newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-ALBORETO GIVES EVIDENCE IN SENNA TRIAL.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ALBORETO GIVES EVIDENCE IN SENNA TRIAL.

text.p: Former Ferrari driver Michele Alboreto told a court on Monday that he believed mechanical failure and not the track was to blame for the crash that killed Ayrton Senna at Imola in 1994.
"I think a mechanical failure caused Senna's accident," said the Italian, winner of five Grands Prix in his career.
Brazilian triple world champion Senna was killed during the San Marino Grand Prix when his Williams car careered off the track at around 210 kph and slammed into a concrete wall.
Team chief Frank Williams and five others are on trial at which all deny charges of manslaughter.
The public prosecutor has blamed a combination of mechanical failure and poor circuit design at the Tamburello curve where the accident happened.

Austrian Roland Ratzenberger died in practice before the race and Alboreto, driving for Minardi, was involved in another incident when his car struck and badly injured a Ferrari mechanic as he accelerated away after a pit stop.

After watching computer-enhanced footage of the Senna crash, Alboreto told the court that from what he had seen it appeared to him that "the swerve on the right of Senna's car makes me think of a mechanical failure".
He said the "slight problems" of the asphalt on the Tamburello were not serious enough to throw a Formula One car off the track.
"There was nothing exceptional at Imola, we raced in a lot worse places," he said.

Pierluigi Martini, another former Minardi driver, told the court last week that some of the drivers had expressed reservations about the surface of the track but added then that he did not think the asphalt had played a part in the crash.
Alboreto pointed out that mechanical failures were normal in the sport, with cars being pushed to their limits.
